records.name: Mauritania
records.summary_text: Mauritania is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely — one of the world's most dangerous legal environments. The 1983 Penal Code criminalises “acts against nature” with death by stoning (de facto moratorium on executions, but the statute is live); and Cairo 52 documents that gender nonconformity is effectively criminalised through debauchery, heresy, and Islamic-morality provisions — trans people can be apprehended solely for their gender expression. There is no LGR, no healthcare, no community, and sharia courts operate alongside the civil system.

records.name: Guinea-Bissau
records.summary_text:
Same-sex conduct is legal — one of few nations in the region never to criminalise it: a 1993 penal code decree omits same-sex offences and a 2014 domestic-violence law protects victims regardless of sexual orientation. No legal gender recognition, no trans framework and no partnership recognition exist, and there is no anti-discrimination protection, so no document or screening pathway for trans travelers is documented.

records.name: Equatorial Guinea
records.summary_text: Equatorial Guinea is dangerous for trans visitors. The 2022 penal code does not explicitly criminalise same-sex conduct — but a 2024 Synergía report documents twelve women imprisoned between January and August 2024 in police raids led by the Armed Forces and State Security, with detention-for-bribes and indefinite imprisonment; a Draft Law “Regulating Prostitution and the Rights of Homosexuals” (2020, status unclear) would formally criminalise. Africa's longest-ruling dictatorship; no recourse.

records.name: Eswatini
records.summary_text: Eswatini is dangerous for trans visitors. Common law criminalises same-sex intimacy; trans people have no access to LGR and limited healthcare; the absolute monarchy punishes dissent harshly (sedition laws; activists assassinated, per BTI 2024); LGBT people face documented discrimination. Eswatini Pride has proceeded annually since 2018 under heavy conditions — a small space of visibility.
